messages:
kevin: Heads-up — after the TS SDK 2.3.0 release we started seeing duplicate quota entries in the dashboard for a small percentage of traffic (~0.12%). Looks correlated with the new routing header name. Can we triage before cutting more SDK releases?

nina: I pulled the dashboard timeseries. There's a clear small bump at 03:14 UTC aligned with the SDK rollout. The parity metric shows 1.12 vs 1.00 tokens/req for affected orgs.

luis: Root cause seems to be that the edge proxy now canonicalizes headers differently and we have both `x-rd-route` (new) and `x-route` (legacy) appearing. Our quota aggregation job treats different header keys as different route identities in the legacy path.

priyanka: Two practical mitigations: (A) quick console-side fix to canonicalize/normalize and collapse equivalent route headers before quota aggregation, (B) SDK-side short-lived workaround to emit the legacy header in addition to the new one behind an opt-in flag. We should avoid silently changing customer-facing behavior.

kevin: Agreed. For (B) I'd rather an explicit opt-in via env var or client config, e.g.:
```js
// TS example
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RDW_KEY, sendLegacyRoute: process.env.SEND_LEGACY_ROUTE === '1' })
```
and in Go:
```go
c := redwood.NewClient(opts.WithSendLegacyRoute(true))
```
We can ship SDK patches that include the flag but keep default false.

nina: On console UX: we should add a small banner on org-level settings if we detect >0.05% requests with mixed header keys advising org admins to coordinate SDK updates. Also add a dashboard tile showing "Route header mix" with a breakdown by SDK language. Query: `sum by(language, header_key) (count_over_time(requests[24h]))`.

luis: I'll follow up in the quota service: add a quick merge step that normalizes keys to lowercase and maps `x-route` and `x-rd-route` to the same canonical key before aggregation. This is low-risk and reversible. I'll do a canary in region-west.

priyanka: Security check: make sure the legacy header doesn't contain anything we treat as a secret. Audit quick scan: route header contains tenant id and route tag only — ok. We'll still add a note in the release notes so SOC folks can review.

kevin: Release plan: cut TS 2.3.1 (docs + opt-in flag), Py 0.19.0 (same opt-in), Go 0.9.4. Coordinate with luis's canary. If console canonicalization goes live first, we can avoid SDK changes but still ship opt-in for safety.

sdk-bot: releasebot: draft release created: TS 2.3.1, Py 0.19.0, Go 0.9.4. CI: all green.

luis: Canaries: quota-normalizer v0.1.1 -> region-west -> monitor 30m. Dependent dashboards updated.

nina: UX tasks: (1) banner copy (short): "Mixed route header formats detected — enable legacy header temporarily or update SDKs. See migration guide." (2) dashboard widget with per-language breakdown (3) alert if mixed>0.1% for >1h. I'll PR content.

kevin: Owners: luis (console normalization canary), kevin (SDK patches + changelogs), nina (banner + dashboard + alert), priyanka (security signoff). Target: canaries in next 6 hours, wide rollouts in 48h if stable.

infra-bot: deploybot: quota-normalizer v0.1.1 canary started in region-west (deploy id dep-2026-03-12-qa).

kevin: One more ask: add an e2e in our SDK test matrix that runs against staging proxy variants (legacy header casing vs normalized) so this doesn't regress. Add it to flaky suppression for now but fail on dup-quota >0.05%.

priyanka: I'll add a lightweight compliance note in SOC docs and tag customers on enterprise plans that could be impacted.

luis: Canary is up. Early metrics look good — mixed header percent dropped after normalizer. Rolling to region-east in 2h if stable.

kevin: Thanks. After we stabilize, let's schedule a deprecation note: remove legacy header emission in SDKs after 30 days post-rollout. We'll announce prominently and email org admins.

nina: +1. Drafting banner copy and migration doc now.

kevin: Great work team. We'll reconvene if we see noise. :rocket:
